review: 116.2b-1: opponent-tries left the Shock outcome unstated; added that the face-down 2/2 dies.
116.2d-1: not-paid delta also changed which lands paid for Rampant Growth; reduced it to the single fact that A does not pay {2}.
116.3-1: illegal-land variant took no special action, so it did not exercise 116.3 (its expected was that nothing changes); dropped it and noted that the rule has no does_not_fire branch.

scenarios.title: A land can be played only with priority, an empty stack, in a main phase of the player's own turn, and once per turn

setup.notes: A has not played a land this turn. The stack is empty and A has priority.

decisions: A has priority and tries to play the Mountain from hand as a special action.

variants.label: base
variants.expected: Playing the Mountain is legal: it moves from A's hand to the battlefield without using the stack, and A has played a land this turn.

variants.label: second-land
variants.delta: A has already played the battlefield Mountain as its land for this turn.
variants.expected: Playing the Mountain from hand is not legal: A has already used the one land play of the turn.

variants.label: stack-not-empty
variants.delta: A has first cast Shock targeting B, tapping the battlefield Mountain, and still holds priority with Shock on the stack.
variants.expected: Playing the Mountain is not legal while Shock is on the stack.

variants.label: combat-step
variants.delta: The step is beginning_of_combat instead of main1.
variants.expected: Playing the Mountain is not legal outside a main phase.

variants.label: opponents-turn
variants.delta: B is the active player and the step is main1; the stack is empty and A holds priority.
variants.expected: Playing the Mountain is not legal: it is not A's turn.

scenarios.title: A face-down creature can be turned face up whenever its controller has priority, without using the stack

setup.notes: The face-down Ainok Tracker is a 2/2 colorless creature with no name or abilities. A has all five Mountains untapped; B's Mountain is untapped.

decisions: B casts Shock targeting A's face-down creature, tapping Mountain, and passes priority.
A receives priority and turns the face-down creature face up by paying its morph cost {4}{R}, tapping five Mountains.
A passes priority, then B passes priority; Shock resolves.

variants.label: base
variants.expected: Turning the creature face up is legal while Shock is on the stack and does not use the stack: Shock is still the only stack object, the creature is Ainok Tracker 3/3 with first strike, and Shock deals 2 damage to it. It stays on the battlefield with 2 damage marked.

variants.label: not-turned
variants.delta: A does not turn the creature face up and passes priority with Shock on the stack.
variants.expected: Shock deals 2 damage to the face-down 2/2 creature, which moves to A's graveyard.

variants.label: cannot-pay
variants.delta: A controls only four Mountains, so the morph cost {4}{R} cannot be paid.
variants.expected: Turning the creature face up is not legal; the creature stays face down and dies to Shock.

variants.label: opponent-tries
variants.delta: B (not the controller) tries to turn A's face-down creature face up instead.
variants.expected: Turning the creature face up is not legal for B; only its controller may take the action. The creature stays face down, and Shock's 2 damage moves the 2/2 to A's graveyard.

scenarios.forge_notes: Requires a face-down permanent in the initial state; a puzzle file can mark it face down with a morph cost.

scenarios.title: A player ends a continuous effect by paying its cost as a special action whenever they have priority

setup.notes: Convulsing Licid has already used its ability: it is a tapped Aura enchantment attached to B's Grizzly Bears, which therefore can't block. A controls an untapped Mountain.

decisions: A, with priority and an empty stack, ends the Licid effect by paying {R}, tapping Mountain.
A moves to combat and attacks B with Hill Giant.
B tries to declare Grizzly Bears as a blocker of Hill Giant.

variants.label: base
variants.expected: Paying {R} is legal and uses no stack: Convulsing Licid stops being an Aura and is a tapped 2/2 Licid creature again, no longer attached. Blocking with Grizzly Bears is legal.

variants.label: not-paid
variants.delta: A does not pay {R}.
variants.expected: Convulsing Licid stays attached to Grizzly Bears, and blocking Hill Giant with Grizzly Bears is not legal.

variants.label: no-mana
variants.delta: A's only Mountain is tapped, so {R} cannot be paid.
variants.expected: Ending the effect is not legal; Convulsing Licid stays attached, and blocking with Grizzly Bears is not legal.

scenarios.forge_notes: Forge may implement the Licid's {R} revert as a stack-using ability or only at certain timings (RevertCost$ on Animate); check whether it is a no-stack action before using this as a ground-truth case. The other branch of 116.2c, stopping a delayed triggered ability from triggering, has no simple Forge card.

scenarios.title: A player ignores a static ability's effect for a duration by paying its cost as a special action

setup.notes: Leonin Arbiter: players can't search libraries; any player may pay {2} for that player to ignore this effect until end of turn.

decisions: A pays {2} to ignore Leonin Arbiter's effect until end of turn, tapping two Mountains (special action; nothing goes on the stack).
A casts Rampant Growth tapping two Forests, and passes priority; B passes priority; Rampant Growth resolves.
A searches for a basic land card and chooses the Forest.

variants.label: base
variants.expected: Rampant Growth resolves: the Forest moves from A's library to the battlefield tapped, and A's library is shuffled.

variants.label: not-paid
variants.delta: A does not pay {2}.
variants.expected: Rampant Growth resolves but A can't search: no land leaves A's library, and A controls no extra land.

variants.label: opponent-pays
variants.delta: B pays {2} (tapping two Plains) to ignore the effect for B, and A does not.
variants.expected: A still can't search: Rampant Growth resolves and nothing leaves A's library. The ignore applies only to the player who paid.

scenarios.forge_notes: The Forge script has a TODO about the AI not using the ignore action; the engine parameter IgnoreEffectCost$ 2 exists for a human-controlled player.

scenarios.title: Circling Vultures can be discarded any time its owner could cast an instant

setup.notes: A holds priority in B's upkeep with an empty stack.

decisions: A, with priority, discards Circling Vultures from hand (cost {0}) as a special action.

variants.label: base
variants.expected: Discarding is legal on the opponent's turn and does not use the stack: Circling Vultures moves from A's hand to A's graveyard and B gets no chance to respond.

variants.label: spell-on-stack
variants.delta: B has cast Shock targeting A, and A has priority with Shock on the stack.
variants.expected: Discarding is legal with a spell on the stack: Circling Vultures moves to A's graveyard, and Shock stays on the stack unchanged.

variants.label: no-priority-step
variants.delta: The step is cleanup, in which no player receives priority.
variants.expected: Discarding is not legal; Circling Vultures stays in A's hand.

scenarios.forge_notes: Forge implements it as an ability with ActivationZone$ Hand and InstantSpeed$ True, which uses the stack in the engine; cleanup priority is only reachable in a puzzle state.

scenarios.title: A card with suspend can be exiled only when it could begin to be cast

setup.notes: A has priority with an empty stack. Rift Bolt is a sorcery with Suspend 1-{R}.

decisions: A, with priority, suspends Rift Bolt by paying {R}, tapping a Mountain, and exiling it.

variants.label: base
variants.expected: Suspending is legal and uses no stack: Rift Bolt moves from A's hand to exile with one time counter.

variants.label: upkeep
variants.delta: The step is upkeep instead of main1.
variants.expected: Suspending is not legal: a sorcery can't be cast in the upkeep. Rift Bolt stays in hand.

variants.label: stack-not-empty
variants.delta: B has cast Shock targeting A, tapping Mountain, and A has priority with Shock on the stack.
variants.expected: Suspending is not legal while the stack is not empty; Rift Bolt stays in hand.

variants.label: opponents-turn
variants.delta: B is the active player and the step is main1.
variants.expected: Suspending is not legal on B's turn; Rift Bolt stays in hand.

scenarios.title: A companion can be put into its owner's hand for {3} only in their main phase with an empty stack

setup.notes: Lurrus of the Dream-Den is A's chosen companion, outside the game. A has not moved a companion to hand this game. The stack is empty and A has priority.

decisions: A, with priority, pays {3} tapping three Plains to put Lurrus of the Dream-Den from outside the game into hand.

variants.label: base
variants.expected: The action is legal and uses no stack: Lurrus moves from outside the game to A's hand, and the three Plains are tapped.

variants.label: combat-step
variants.delta: The step is beginning_of_combat instead of main1.
variants.expected: The action is not legal outside a main phase; Lurrus stays outside the game.

variants.label: stack-not-empty
variants.delta: B has cast Shock targeting A and A has priority with Shock on the stack.
variants.expected: The action is not legal with a spell on the stack; Lurrus stays outside the game.

variants.label: opponents-turn
variants.delta: B is the active player and the step is main1.
variants.expected: The action is not legal on B's turn; Lurrus stays outside the game.

variants.label: cannot-pay
variants.delta: A controls only two Plains.
variants.expected: The action is not legal: {3} can't be paid; Lurrus stays outside the game.

scenarios.forge_notes: Companion setup needs the companion in the player's outside-the-game zone (sideboard); Forge supports it in constructed games with a companion declared.

scenarios.title: A card with foretell can be exiled face down for {2} during its controller's turn whenever they have priority

setup.notes: A has priority with an empty stack.

decisions: A, with priority, pays {2} tapping two Islands to foretell Behold the Multiverse (exile it face down).

variants.label: base
variants.expected: Foretelling is legal and uses no stack: Behold the Multiverse moves from A's hand to exile face down, and two Islands are tapped.

variants.label: stack-not-empty
variants.delta: A has first cast Shock targeting B, tapping Mountain, and still holds priority with Shock on the stack.
variants.expected: Foretelling is legal with Shock on the stack; Behold the Multiverse moves to exile face down and Shock is unchanged on the stack.

variants.label: opponents-turn
variants.delta: B is the active player and the step is main1; A holds priority with an empty stack.
variants.expected: Foretelling is not legal on B's turn; Behold the Multiverse stays in hand.

variants.label: cannot-pay
variants.delta: A controls only one land, an Island.
variants.expected: Foretelling is not legal: {2} can't be paid; Behold the Multiverse stays in hand.

scenarios.title: A card with plot can be exiled only in the owner's own turn with priority and an empty stack

setup.notes: A has priority with an empty stack.

decisions: A, with priority, pays the plot cost {1}{R} tapping two Mountains to plot Slickshot Show-Off (exile it from hand).

variants.label: base
variants.expected: Plotting is legal and uses no stack: Slickshot Show-Off moves from A's hand to exile as a plotted card.

variants.label: stack-not-empty
variants.delta: B has cast Shock targeting A, tapping Mountain, and A has priority with Shock on the stack.
variants.expected: Plotting is not legal while the stack is not empty; Slickshot Show-Off stays in hand.

variants.label: opponents-turn
variants.delta: B is the active player and the step is main1.
variants.expected: Plotting is not legal on B's turn; Slickshot Show-Off stays in hand.

scenarios.forge_notes: Rule 702.170a limits plotting to the owner's main phase with an empty stack, stricter than 116.2k's 'during their own turn'; no variant here relies on the difference (an upkeep plot is left out).

scenarios.title: A locked half of a Room can be unlocked by paying its unlock cost only in a main phase of own turn with an empty stack

setup.notes: Bottomless Pool // Locker Room is on the battlefield with the Bottomless Pool door unlocked and the Locker Room door locked. A has five untapped Islands and priority with an empty stack.

decisions: A, with priority, pays the unlock cost {4}{U} of Locker Room tapping five Islands to unlock it.

variants.label: base
variants.expected: Unlocking is legal and uses no stack: the Locker Room door becomes unlocked and all five Islands are tapped.

variants.label: combat-step
variants.delta: The step is beginning_of_combat instead of main1.
variants.expected: Unlocking is not legal outside a main phase; the Locker Room door stays locked.

variants.label: stack-not-empty
variants.delta: B has cast Shock targeting A and A has priority with Shock on the stack.
variants.expected: Unlocking is not legal while the stack is not empty; the door stays locked.

variants.label: opponents-turn
variants.delta: B is the active player and the step is main1.
variants.expected: Unlocking is not legal on B's turn; the door stays locked.

scenarios.forge_notes: Room cards are listed by their first-door Name line; the second door is named Locker Room. The Room-unlocked state must be settable in the initial state.

scenarios.title: A player who takes a special action receives priority afterward

setup.notes: A has priority with an empty stack and has not played a land this turn.

decisions: A plays Mountain from hand as a special action.
A then casts Shock targeting B, tapping the Mountain just played.

variants.label: base
variants.expected: A holds priority after playing the Mountain: the step is still main1, B received no priority, and A's Shock is cast (on the stack) with no pass in between.

variants.label: passes
variants.delta: After playing the Mountain, A passes priority instead of casting Shock.
variants.expected: B receives priority with an empty stack; when B also passes, the game moves to beginning_of_combat. A did not keep priority once A passed.

scenarios.forge_notes: 116.3 applies after every special action without condition, so it has no does_not_fire variant; the contrast is the 'passes' variant, where priority leaves A only once A passes.
